title: Reporting Advice with Had Better — Quiz 134
content:
## Reporting Advice with Had Better

Change advice with had better into indirect speech.

### Lesson focus

1. He said, “You had better consult a doctor.”
2. The doctor said, “You had better take rest.”

### Understand the pattern

Had better expresses fairly strong advice about a specific situation. It can stay had better in a reported clause. Another natural report uses advised + person + to-infinitive; the choice should preserve the intended advice.

### Worked answers and explanation

He said, 'You had better consult a doctor' → He advised the listener to consult a doctor. The doctor said, 'You had better rest' → The doctor advised the patient to rest. These grammatical reports do not establish a diagnosis or replace professional advice.

### Try another

Report: She said to me, 'You had better leave early.'

### Suggested answer

She advised me to leave early. Alternatively, she told me that I had better leave early. Do not change had better into 'would better'.
